newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada criticizes U.S. move against Sherritt.
newsitem.headline: Canada criticizes U.S. move against Sherritt.

text.p: Canadian International Trade Minister Art Eggleton criticized further Cuban-related moves by the United States against Sherritt International Corp on Friday as a violation of trade rules.
"I think it's a sorry situation, and I think it continues to be a violation of trade rules," Eggleton told reporters.

The State Department said four more Sherritt executives would be banned from entering the United States under the Helms-Burton law because of company operations in Cuba. A total of 11 executives have now been barred, it said.
Eggleton said the United States was reaching a "new low" by "getting down to the employee level" at Sherritt.

He said Canada would pursue its strategy of joining the European Union (EU) in its World Trade Organization challenge of Helms-Burton, and suggested the EU had gained nothing in its private discussions with Washington on the issue.
He repeated that Canada did not rule out requesting a panel under the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), which groups Canada, the United States and Mexico.

Another irritant regarding Cuba has involved Wal-Mart Stores Inc, whose Canadian subsidiary pulled Cuban-made pajamas from its shelves but then announced under Canadian government pressure that it would again sell them.
A U.S. Treasury official said on Friday that Washington was interested in enforcing an embargo against any U.S.-owned company's trade with Cuba.
Eggleton said it was important that Washington realized that Wal-Mart Canada was a Canadian company that had to obey Canadian laws, and he said he hoped the United States would not levy penalties.
"I hope they wouldn't do that," he said.
